settings.title: Basic hand tools
settings.description: A hacksaw, files, sandpaper, a measuring tape — no power tools. Everything else is in the kit.

settings.title: A bit of space
settings.description: A sturdy table around 1200 × 600 mm and a spot the frame can sit undisturbed while joints cure.

settings.title: A few weekends
settings.description: 25–35 hours across multiple sessions. No rush — bamboo is forgiving and most mistakes are fixable.

settings.title: Set the geometry
settings.description: Lock gravel geometry on the jig — wider clearance and a slacker head angle than road.

settings.title: Join & wrap
settings.description: Bond the tubes with epoxy and wrap each joint with carbon-fibre tow.

settings.title: Cure
settings.description: Leave it for a full cure — that's where maximum joint strength comes from.

settings.title: Sand, seal & ride
settings.description: Sand smooth, seal the bamboo, fit headset and BB. Adventure awaits.

settings.quote: I've got five bikes and this is my favourite — it feels stiffer, dampens vibration better, and I feel safer and more confident on it.

settings.question: Can a bamboo frame really handle proper trail riding?
settings.answer: Yes. Bamboo's natural damping is a real advantage on rough terrain, and the bonded joints are stronger than the tubes themselves. Riders hit singletrack, roots and drops on BBC hardtails regularly. Tested with Swansea University, under 1% failure across 4,000+ builds since 2012.

settings.question: Is it stiff enough to climb and put power down?
settings.answer: The MTB kit uses bigger-diameter bamboo tubes and tighter tolerances than our road and gravel kits, built for off-road loads. Builders report it climbs well and descends confidently — 'the 29er geometry is spot on.'

settings.question: Will it survive impacts and rough terrain?
settings.answer: Bamboo is a natural composite at roughly 28,000 PSI tensile strength — comparable to mild steel but lighter. Unlike carbon it doesn't fail catastrophically on a hard hit, and any damage can be repaired with epoxy anywhere in the world.

settings.question: What wheel size and brakes does it take?
settings.answer: It's built around 29er geometry with disc-brake mounts and a BSA 68mm bottom bracket. Our MTB component pack is specced for 650B/27.5" if you prefer the smaller, punchier wheel — your call.

settings.question: How long does the MTB frame take to build?
settings.answer: About 30–45 hours over a few weekends — a little longer than our road and gravel kits because the tubes are larger and the off-road tolerances are tighter. No power tools needed: just basic hand tools and a work surface.

settings.product_subtitle: Bigger bamboo tubes, tighter tolerances and disc-ready 29er geometry — built by hand to take roots, rocks and drops. Bamboo's natural damping kills trail chatter the way an alloy frame never will, and the joints are stronger than the tubes.
